**A-1 Pictures, Inc.** (Japanese: 株式会社A-1 Pictures, Hepburn: _Kabushiki-gaisha Ē-wan Pikuchāzu_) is a Japanese animation studio and production company founded by ex-Sunrise producer Mikihiro Iwata. It is a subsidiary of Sony Music Entertainment Japan's animation production firm Aniplex.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-offsite-greeting-jp-10)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-offsite-greeting-en-11)
The company was established by SMEJ's animation production division, Aniplex, on May 9, 2005, to animate its animated series and productions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-offsite-greeting-jp-10)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-offsite-greeting-en-11) In 2006, it co-produced the original production _Zenmai Zamurai_, and in October of the same year, established a studio in Asagaya. In the following year, 2007, the studio produced its first series, _Ōkiku Furikabutte_.
Originally established to oversee the production of only a few of Aniplex's family-oriented series, the studio has since grown and expanded as a full-fledged studio involved in the production of a wide range of media and animation productions and other activities, which it has overseen. The studio has also expanded its international presence, participating in the noted international convention, Anime Expo 2007 (AX 2007), held in Long Beach, California, and having its own panel there.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-axpanel-advanced-12)

In 2010, A-1 Pictures worked in collaboration with a joint project of TV Tokyo's animation department and Aniplex called Anime no Chikara for the creation of original animated series.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-AnC_announced-13) Three animated series were produced that year for the project: _Sound of the Sky_, _Night Raid 1931_ and _Occult Academy_.
In April 2018, A-1 Pictures rebranded its Kōenji Studio as CloverWorks, giving it a unique brand identity, which made it distinguishable from its main Asagaya Studio.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-CloverWorks-14)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-15) On October 1, 2018, CloverWorks separated from A-1 Pictures, although it still remains as a subsidiary under Aniplex.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-16)
On June 17, 2024, the studio 3Hz announced that its animation planning and production business was transferred to A-1 Pictures.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-17)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-18)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Pictures#cite_note-19)

A-1 Pictures (A-1 Pictures Inc.) is a Japanese animation studio in Suginami, Tokyo. Founded by former Sunrise producer Mikihiro Iwata in 2005, it was established as a subsidary of Aniplex. The studio was meant to oversee Aniplex's family-oriented series before it evolved into producing various independent anime projects.  
A-1 Pictures has since released popular television anime such as Fairy Tail, Sword Art Online, Nanatsu no Taizai (The Seven Deadly Sins), and Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai: Tensai-tachi no Renai Zunousen (Kaguya-Sama: Love is War).

Title: Greatest A-1 Pictures Anime Series
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
**A-1 Pictures is a Japanese animation studio** that was founded in 2005, and it has produced dozens of anime series, OVAs, and movies. It does not get as much praise as Mappa, Toei, and Ufotable, but A-1 Pictures has developed a healthy reputation within the anime community for its quality and production. Not every series is a home-run, but A-1 Pictures has produced some great anime content.
The **best anime from A-1 Pictures typically targets younger audiences**, but certain series are darker and more mature than others. Many of these anime are based on manga or another type of source material, but a few are original works that were created by A-1 Pictures. Whether it is a shonen, a mech series, or a romance story, A-1 Pictures genuinely does a great job of bringing anime to life.
_**Updated on October 27, 2024 by Robbie Robinson:** A-1 Pictures has produced a great number of fantastic anime. Whether they're original anime or adaptations of manga, A-1 has proven their mettle in the anime industry. This list has been updated to include more of their best anime series and to get this article up CBR's current formatting standards._

## 15  Mashle: Magic and Muscles Puts a Spin On a School For Magic
### Based on the Manga by Hajime Kōmoto
_Mashle_ has often been looked at as a silly spoof of _Harry Potter_. While there are certainly aspects of that, it's far more entertaining than just being compared to a goofy Hogwarts. In a society that values magical strength and power over anything else, Mash Burnedead is incapable of using magic. Sick of the societal expectations, Mash decides it's time to show the world that there are different kinds of strength. _Physical_ strength, in particular.
_Mashle: Magic and Muscles_ might be taking the last place on this list, but that doesn't mean it isn't a great show. It's wildly entertaining watching Mash use his raw strength to prove himself time and time again. Usually, an overpowered protagonist in a world of magic is the strongest magic user around. Not in this anime. It's a fun take on the genre of magic schools, and Mash stands out as a great main character to follow.
**Release Date** 2023 - 2024-00-00
**Network** Tokyo MX, Gunma TV, BS11, Tochigi TV
**Directors** Aya Ikeda, Jun Takahashi, Harume Kosaka, Naoaki Shibuta
**Writers** Riichiro Inagaki
**Franchise(s)** Eyeshield 21
*   Chiaki Kobayashi
Mash Burnedead (voice)
*   Reiji Kawashima
Finn Ames (voice)

## 14  Lycoris Recoil Is Gun Fights With a Beating Heart At Its Core
### Original Series Created by Spider Lily and Asaura
Releasing in 2022, _Lycoris Recoil_ was a welcome surprise from A-1. The Direct Attack group recruits orphaned girls and turns them into deadly assassins. Takina Inoue is a tad too trigger-happy when it comes to missions, which causes plenty of strife with her team. She is then partnered with another girl, Chisato Nishikigi, working under Lycoris, the name dedicated to the young girls. In between missions, Chisato and Takina spend their daily lives working at a café.
While the shoot-outs are extraordinarily well done, the greatest part of _Lycoris Recoil_ is the growing relationship between Takina and Chisato. Chisato refuses to take a life, even if it's at the cost of her own. Takina, on the other hand, is the complete opposite. The series perfectly portrays the trope of a self-sacrificing hero and their partner who would do anything to save them from their fate. With impressive visuals and an expertly explored relationship, **_Lycoris Recoil_ is, without a doubt, one of A-1 Pictures best series.**
**Release Date** 2022 - 2022
*   Lizzie Freeman   
*   Xanthe Huynh
In a downtown Tokyo café, a group of girls will help sort out any problems to help the local customers.
**Main Genre**Animation
**Seasons** 1
**Studio** A-1 Pictures
**Number of Episodes** 13

## 13  NieR:Automata Ver1.1a Excels At Storytelling
### Based on the Video Game by PlatinumGames
Image via Crunchyroll
A-1 impressed countless fans of _Nier_ with its anime adaptation. Following an otherworldly invasion enforced by alien machines, the earth has fallen into a post-apocalyptic state. Humanity's final line of defense is a militaristic group of androids working under YoRHa. 2B, a martial fighter combat unit, and 9S, an android that specializes in hacking, are sent to earth for a mission. There, the story unfolds into a bittersweet tale of morality concerning both the androids _and_ the alien machines.
Not only does A-1 do an exceptional job at retaining the weight and emotions of the video game, but they've actually expanded upon the world and stories in glorious fashions. It's one of the best series adaptations of a video game seen in recent years and can be enjoyed by even those who have never played the game. It has stellar visuals and combat sequences, but _NieR_'s strongest point is its narrative.
**Release Date** January 8, 2023
**Directors** Ryouji Masuyama
**Writers** Ryouji Masuyama, Yoko Taro
*   Yui Ishikawa   
*   Natsuki Hanae   
*   Hiroki Yasumoto   
*   Kaoru Akiyama
**Seasons** 1
**Story By** Yoko Taro

## 12  Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day Is a Notorious Tear-Jerker
### Original Series Created by Super Peace Busters
Image via A-1 Pictures
If there's one thing that's absolutely certain about _Anohana_, it's that it can be an incredibly sad watch. After a young girl, Meiko "Menma" Honma dies, her group of friends begin to drift apart. Years later, the anime follows Menma's friend, Jinta Yadomi. Haunted by the loss of his friend, he has become rather reclusive. However, Menma then actually appears to him, telling Jinta that she's unable to completely pass on.
Thus, Jinta must try to regroup his old friends in order to help Menma properly move on to the other side. _Anohana_ is a heavy-hitter as it tackles themes of grief and loss. It's really well done, making _Anohana_ an amazing show for anyone who has suffered from losing someone important to them. A-1 Pictures knocked it out of the park with this anime, as _Anohana_ is a gorgeous story of moving forward that will bring all viewers to tears at one point or another.

## 15  Mashle: Magic and Muscles Puts a Spin On a School For Magic
### Based on the Manga by Hajime Kōmoto
_Mashle_ has often been looked at as a silly spoof of _Harry Potter_. While there are certainly aspects of that, it's far more entertaining than just being compared to a goofy Hogwarts. In a society that values magical strength and power over anything else, Mash Burnedead is incapable of using magic. Sick of the societal expectations, Mash decides it's time to show the world that there are different kinds of strength. _Physical_ strength, in particular.
_Mashle: Magic and Muscles_ might be taking the last place on this list, but that doesn't mean it isn't a great show. It's wildly entertaining watching Mash use his raw strength to prove himself time and time again. Usually, an overpowered protagonist in a world of magic is the strongest magic user around. Not in this anime. It's a fun take on the genre of magic schools, and Mash stands out as a great main character to follow.
**Release Date** 2023 - 2024-00-00
**Network** Tokyo MX, Gunma TV, BS11, Tochigi TV
**Directors** Aya Ikeda, Jun Takahashi, Harume Kosaka, Naoaki Shibuta
**Writers** Riichiro Inagaki
**Franchise(s)** Eyeshield 21

Mash Burnedead (voice)
*   Reiji Kawashima
Finn Ames (voice)

## 14  Lycoris Recoil Is Gun Fights With a Beating Heart At Its Core
### Original Series Created by Spider Lily and Asaura
Releasing in 2022, _Lycoris Recoil_ was a welcome surprise from A-1. The Direct Attack group recruits orphaned girls and turns them into deadly assassins. Takina Inoue is a tad too trigger-happy when it comes to missions, which causes plenty of strife with her team. She is then partnered with another girl, Chisato Nishikigi, working under Lycoris, the name dedicated to the young girls. In between missions, Chisato and Takina spend their daily lives working at a café.
While the shoot-outs are extraordinarily well done, the greatest part of _Lycoris Recoil_ is the growing relationship between Takina and Chisato. Chisato refuses to take a life, even if it's at the cost of her own. Takina, on the other hand, is the complete opposite. The series perfectly portrays the trope of a self-sacrificing hero and their partner who would do anything to save them from their fate. With impressive visuals and an expertly explored relationship, **_Lycoris Recoil_ is, without a doubt, one of A-1 Pictures best series.**
**Release Date** 2022 - 2022
*   Lizzie Freeman   
*   Xanthe Huynh
In a downtown Tokyo café, a group of girls will help sort out any problems to help the local customers.

**Seasons** 1
**Studio** A-1 Pictures
**Number of Episodes** 13

## 13  NieR:Automata Ver1.1a Excels At Storytelling
### Based on the Video Game by PlatinumGames
Image via Crunchyroll
A-1 impressed countless fans of _Nier_ with its anime adaptation. Following an otherworldly invasion enforced by alien machines, the earth has fallen into a post-apocalyptic state. Humanity's final line of defense is a militaristic group of androids working under YoRHa. 2B, a martial fighter combat unit, and 9S, an android that specializes in hacking, are sent to earth for a mission. There, the story unfolds into a bittersweet tale of morality concerning both the androids _and_ the alien machines.
Not only does A-1 do an exceptional job at retaining the weight and emotions of the video game, but they've actually expanded upon the world and stories in glorious fashions. It's one of the best series adaptations of a video game seen in recent years and can be enjoyed by even those who have never played the game. It has stellar visuals and combat sequences, but _NieR_'s strongest point is its narrative.

## 12  Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day Is a Notorious Tear-Jerker
### Original Series Created by Super Peace Busters
Image via A-1 Pictures
If there's one thing that's absolutely certain about _Anohana_, it's that it can be an incredibly sad watch. After a young girl, Meiko "Menma" Honma dies, her group of friends begin to drift apart. Years later, the anime follows Menma's friend, Jinta Yadomi. Haunted by the loss of his friend, he has become rather reclusive. However, Menma then actually appears to him, telling Jinta that she's unable to completely pass on.
Thus, Jinta must try to regroup his old friends in order to help Menma properly move on to the other side. _Anohana_ is a heavy-hitter as it tackles themes of grief and loss. It's really well done, making _Anohana_ an amazing show for anyone who has suffered from losing someone important to them. A-1 Pictures knocked it out of the park with this anime, as _Anohana_ is a gorgeous story of moving forward that will bring all viewers to tears at one point or another.
